title: MEM-64M: a 64 MiB private working set, reclaimed and re-served twenty times
body:
## Change
Close MEM-64M's last open exit condition: twenty spawn/grow/exit-or-fault cycles at the declared 64 MiB ceiling, with no downward drift in reusable memory, slots, or accounting, and no stale data exposure.

A new composition `sel4-private-memory-cycles` (generation 55) has `init` relaunch one declared 16384-page holder twenty times — ten ending by clean exit, ten by a deliberate write past the window. Each incarnation reads all 16384 of its pages as zero, stamps each with a value no other incarnation writes, then reads every stamp back. The reuse qualification runs as a `--arm cycles` arm of the existing private-memory checker, behind the new `just private_memory_cycles_check`.

A separate composition is forced rather than chosen: `PrivateMemoryBudget::validate_against` sums *declared* quotas, and `sel4-private-memory` already declares 32280 of the target's 32768-page aggregate, so a 16384-page holder beside them is refused at admission before anything runs.

## Claim and limits
The reuse clause is observed on `qemu-arm-virt`. It names no architecture; the milestone's grow-to-ceiling condition, which `private_memory_check` already observes on both, is unchanged at 24 markers.

The arm is closure-backed and AArch64 only. The RV64 private-memory image is still built through a legacy `build-sel4.py` plane flag that CP15 is retiring, and extending that surface to reach a second architecture this clause does not ask for would add work to the deletion.

This PR does not claim the 256 MiB/1 GiB envelope, concurrent holders across repeated lives, or physical-machine qualification — MEM-1G owns those with its own evidence.

## Risk and review surface
- `components/testkit/private-cycle-probe/src/main.rs`: the three-pass touch. Reading every page before writing any, and reading the stamps back afterwards, is the assertion; fusing the write into the first pass would let an aliased page satisfy its own check.
- `components/system/init/src/main.rs`: `drive_private_memory_cycles_plane` asserts each holder ended by the path its cycle parity names, so a probe that stopped faulting cannot pass by terminating cleanly twenty times.
- `scripts/check/check-sel4-private-memory-plane.py`: `check_reuse_cycles` asserts exact equality of the allocator's own watermarks across cycles, not a tolerance. `check_markers` is now arm-scoped; the module's `CHAINS` union exists only for the meta-gate's coverage pin.
- `boot-contracts/src/generation.rs`: `BootAction::PrivateMemoryCycles = 39`, reaching `ALL`, `from_id`, `parse`, and the frozen numbering table.
- The 54 churned closure records are identity propagation: `init` and `boot-contracts` are tree inputs to every closure and both changed.

## The fault decode gap
The fault chain pins `kind=VirtualMemory` but deliberately leaves the access field open, and this is a real limitation rather than a loose pattern.

The probe's store does trap — its "did not trap" report never appears — but this configuration reports `access: Execute status: 0`. The pre-existing `reclamation-fault` probe produces exactly the same shape for its own deliberate write (`SLIME_GRAPH component fault task=81 kind=VirtualMemory { access: Execute, status: 0 } address=Some(67108864)`), so this is `normalize_vm_access` failing to hit either data-abort exception class, not this probe. Asserting `Write` would pin behaviour the platform does not produce; ending the pattern at `kind=` accepted an *accidental* prefetch fault and so observed no deliberate fault at all, which is how the first revision passed. The clause is instead carried by each faulting holder having reported a fully committed quota first. Left as a `slime-root/src/fault.rs` follow-up.

## Verification
Observed on this tree during the change, not a separate post-commit CI run:
- `just private_memory_cycles_check`: passed — `11 markers across 4 causal chains and 1 image case on qemu-arm-virt`.
- Per-cycle drift: all twenty holder censuses identical at `slots=522045 bytes=1515227504 live_objects=145`; `extent_reuses` 65 → 1235, +65 per cycle.
- Per-cycle backing: twenty of `delta=16384 previous=0 pages=16384 base=0x4000000 large_frames=32 base_frames=0 leaf_tables=0` — one base for every incarnation.
- Terminal: `spawns served=20 drops=0 terminated=21`; `mapped_ram=0 reusable_private_ram=67239936 allocation_descriptors_free=288416`; `SLIME_GRAPH HEALTHY generation=55`.
- `just private_memory_check`: passed on both architectures, unchanged at 24 markers across 8 chains.
- `just sel4_gate_control_check`: 48 gates, 1963 mutated transcripts (1937 before), so every new marker is mutation-covered.
- `just test_sel4_root` 240/240; `just test_host` 342 boot-contracts tests including the extended frozen boot-action table.
- `just contracts_check` (42 manifests), `just component_spec_check` (84 records, 43 mutations refused), `just component_crate_split_check` (76 crates), `just system_spec_check` (45 systems, 21 refused).
- `just system_image_closure_check`, `just system_test_run_check` (51 records), `just system_image_closure_aggregate_check` (all 54 closures exercised by an owning gate).
- `just fmt_check_all`, `just lint_all`, `just ruff`, `just typos`, `just machete`, `just devlog_check`, `just tasks_check`: passed.

Two defects were found and fixed during implementation, both mine: the first run refused `21 reclamation census record(s), expected 20` because init's own exit is reclaimed too, and the ceiling arm's summary had begun reporting the union marker count, claiming the cycles arm's evidence for a run that never booted its image.

## Evidence
The [private reuse-cycles entry](devlog/2026-09-13-mem-64m-private-reuse-cycles/index.md) records the change, the decisions, and the open follow-ups, with the passing run's full 3182-line serial capture as [`private-memory-cycles-plane.log`](devlog/2026-09-13-mem-64m-private-reuse-cycles/private-memory-cycles-plane.log). MEM-64M's work item carries the observed results and is closed.

title: Closure identity: a tree input is its content, not its checkout
body:
## Change

A system image closure's tree inputs are now identified by their content with repository metadata excluded: `tree_identity` in `scripts/lib/system_image_closure.py` digests with `.git` excluded, and the generator resolves tree inputs through it instead of calling `tree_digest` directly. All 59 closures in the v2 corpus (53 canonical, 6 negative) are regenerated, each moving only its kernel-loader identity, and the 50 test-run records are re-frozen to the closure identities they now compile to (46 move; the 4 closure-exempt runs name none). The closure checker gains `check_repository_metadata`: two trees differing only in their `.git` file share an identity, and a content edit changes it.

Closes work item `01a09118-1086-78e6-b8aa-f25920b8992d`. Record: `devlog/2026-09-12-closure-gitlink-identity/`.

## Claim

A closure identity depends on the bytes a clone reproduces, not on how the checkout was made. Before this change every closure named its loader by a digest that included the submodule's `.git` gitlink, whose content is a relative path into the superproject's object store, so `generate-system-image-closures.py --check` reported all 50 closures stale from any `git worktree` of the same commit.

## Risk

Low. Only `.git` is excluded, so an uncommitted edit inside a submodule still changes the identity. The regenerated identities are the intended recomputation and nothing else: every closure diff is one loader-identity line, and every test-run diff is one `imageClosureIdentity` line.

## Review surface

- `scripts/lib/system_image_closure.py`: `REPOSITORY_METADATA` and `tree_identity`.
- `scripts/generate/generate-system-image-closures.py`: `identity_of` now calls `tree_identity`.

- `contracts/system-image-closure/v2/{closures,negative}/` and `contracts/system-test-run/v1/runs/`: generated, one line each.

## Claim

A component on Slime OS opens a TCP connection to its one generation-declared destination, sends 4096 bytes, and reads them back byte for byte, over the IO3 virtio-net driver and smoltcp inside `network-service`. On the `sel4-io-tcp` plane the probe's stream is verified with zero mismatches; its connect to a second declared port comes back `refused` on the peer's RST; its connect to an undeclared host is denied before any frame leaves; the peer's frame ledger agrees with the service's socket counters; and the graph ends healthy. `just io_tcp_check` observes all of it. IO11 closes on that observation; IO10 stays open for the board lane (P6.F).

This is the lane's second session; rebased onto main after #30 (the link attachment) merged.

A client's delegated loans become its IO0 data queue; `OP_SEND`/`OP_RECV` are admitted in the authority order (decode → capability and holder → right → direction, byte budget, page bounds → queue depth) before a byte touches a socket. title: Verification gates: memoize zutai evaluations by content and prefetch them in parallel
body:
## Why

Every contract gate ran `zutai-cli` once per spec, serially and from scratch, and each script in a stacked recipe repeated the whole pass. Only the system-spec checker is expensive (about 8 s and 1.6 GB per evaluation against tens of milliseconds for the others), so a one-line component change paid several six-minute passes before its one-second QEMU plane could boot. Work item `01a090af-08a4-763b-8a9f-76b7d6376dd4` records the measured wall times.

## What changed

- `scripts/lib/zutai_cli.py`: `evaluate` memoizes each evaluation's stdout under `build/zutai-cache/`, keyed by the content of everything that determines it: the binary, the stdlib, every `.zt` and `zutai.zti` package manifest under `contracts/`, the module itself, the checker's repository-relative path, the command, the env var name, and the input bytes. The input's path is never in the key, only a zero exit is stored, and a store that cannot be read or written is skipped rather than fatal. `prefetch` fills the cache for a corpus on a thread pool sized `min(cpu_count, MemAvailable // 2 GiB)`, or `SLIME_ZUTAI_JOBS`. `SLIME_ZUTAI_CACHE=0` is exactly the previous path.
- The four `_run_zutai` helpers (`system_spec`, `component_spec`, `interface_schema`, `system_image_closure`) route through `evaluate` with signatures, pre-checks, and messages unchanged; `system_spec.prefetch_systems` warms a set of systems.
- One `prefetch_systems(...)` line before the existing corpus-scale serial loop in `check-system-spec.py`, `check-system-image-builder.py`, `check-system-image-scenario.py`, `generate-generation-from-spec.py`, and `generate-system-image-closures.py`. The loops, their order, and their error attribution do not change. `resolve_closure` admits the component corpus once per closure instead of twice.
- Devlog `devlog/2026-09-11-zutai-gate-cache/` with the measurements and evidence; the item closed on them; a new deferred backlog item for a defect found while verifying (below).

## Invariants / risk

- Outputs are byte-identical to the serial path by construction: only the source of the stdout string changed. A cache key that omitted an input would let a stale result through, so the key covers everything `zutai-cli run` reads: the input, every `.zt` and package manifest under `contracts/` (the CLI discovers its package graph from those manifests on every run), the stdlib, and the binary's content; the checker's path is included because sibling checkers share a directory.
- Parallelism cannot change what a gate reports: a failed prefetch job is left for the serial pass, which re-runs it and reports it in today's order and text.
- The store holds verbatim tool stdout under the gitignored `build/`; it is a memo, not a persisted format, so it defines no schema. `rm -rf build/zutai-cache` resets it; the key's format tag orphans old entries when the recipe changes.
- No `just` recipe, contract, or Rust changed; no new check script. CI (`contracts_check`, `component_spec_check`) sees a cold cache each run and no prefetch, so its behavior is unchanged apart from writing under `build/`.

## Verification

Measured with `SLIME_ZUTAI_JOBS=2` while another session ran the serial generators on the same 16-core, 14 GB host, so every figure is an upper bound.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| sha256 of every routed zutai stdout over 43 systems, 82 components, 4 interfaces, 50 closures and the test runs (224 rows), serial vs cold vs warm | identical; the `SLIME_ZUTAI_CACHE=0` run wrote no entries |
| `check-system-spec.py` serial / cold / warm | 664 s / 518 s / 3.1 s, `contracts/` unmodified (1.1 s warm after review fixes) |
| `generate-generation-from-spec.py --check` serial / warm | 512 s / 1.7 s (0.3 s after review fixes) |
| `generate-system-image-closures.py --check` serial / cold / warm | 598 s / 316 s / 7.7 s (rc 1 in all three for the worktree defect below, not this change) |
| Warm-cache refusals after a `bootAttempts` edit in `sel4-channel.zti` | generator: only that fixture stale; checker: `manifest.health.bootAttempts: 4 != 3`; closure check: `systemSpec: identity mismatch`; a spec with garbage appended is refused twice with no entry written |
| `just contracts_check` | pass (825 s, first run in a fresh worktree) |
| `just system_spec_check` warm | pass, 190 s end to end (158 s after review fixes), nearly all the untouched `contracts_check` prefix (the item recorded 21 min) |
| Store made unreadable and unwritable, one evaluation | rc 0, result returned |
| `just component_crate_split_check`, `just ruff`, `just typos`, `just devlog_check`, `just tasks_check` | pass |

The item's two-minute bound holds for the two scripts `system_spec_check` adds, not for the recipe, whose prefix this change does not touch; the item body records that amendment and the follow-up carries the prefix. No Rust changed and no QEMU plane was run.

## Related

- `01a090af-08a4-763b-8a9f-76b7d6376dd4` — closed on the observations above.
- `01a0915e-d8a1-722b-91e4-cb3ec57c6632` — follow-up for the `contracts_check` prefix that now dominates `system_spec_check`.
- `01a09118-1086-78e6-b8aa-f25920b8992d` — found while verifying from a git worktree: every closure digests `deps/rust-sel4` including its `.git` gitlink, so the closure generator's `--check` reports all 50 stale in any worktree (the primary checkout's loader digest equals the committed identity; both agree with `.git` excluded). Filed as backlog and deferred with its rationale so `tasks_check` stays green; reopen if you would rather it stay open.

title: IO11: the network service attaches to virtio-net and answers ARP and ICMP under QEMU
body:
## Claim

`network-service` attaches to the IO3 virtio-net driver and runs a bounded smoltcp IPv4 stack behind the exact-destination authority it already enforces. On the new `sel4-io-tcp` plane (generation 54) it configures its generation-declared interface, answers ARP and ICMP echo from a frame-level peer the gate controls, holds one client's exact destination, and releases the link through the driver's reset handshake. `just io_tcp_check` observes all of it; `just io_network_check` and `just io_link_check` are unchanged and green.

This is the first of the lane's sessions (IO11): the link attachment. The TCP byte stream (active open, send, receive, close) is the next PR.

## Change

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `contracts/syscall-abi/v1` (70, 71), `slime-root` | `CLOCK RATE READ`: the counter's rate under `monotonicRead`. `CAPABILITY NETWORK INTERFACE READ`: the interface table on the destination read's exact shape and identity gate. Root test count 215. |
| `contracts/network-interface/v1`, `boot-contracts`, builder, system-spec | One static IPv4 interface per holder (address, prefix, gateway, MAC), validated at build and decode; optional spec fields, so no earlier spec or baseline changes. |
| `components/services/network-service` | `link.rs`: smoltcp `Device` over the IO3 client shape; `main.rs`: interface read, clock, optional link attachment, polling loop, reset-handshake release. smoltcp 0.13.0 (0BSD, with `managed`) in `deny.toml`. |
| `components/lib` | `link_frames.rs` (slot tracking) and `tick_clock.rs` (tick arithmetic), host-tested. |
| `components/testkit/io-tcp-probe`, `sel4-io-tcp` | The client and the data-plane composition; generation 53 keeps its loopback and baseline. |
| `scripts/lib/link_peer.py`, `scripts/check/check-sel4-io-network-plane.py --arm tcp`, `just io_tcp_check`, `just link_peer_check` | A frame-level peer on QEMU's UDP socket backend with a ledger the gate cross-checks; the peer's own host regressions; gate-control pin 16 → 39. |
| `.tasks/items/`, `devlog/` | IO10 (epic), IO11 (active), P6.F; the lane's Decision entry with its plan of record; the Change entry with the passing plane's serial transcript. |

## Risk

Root changes are two mechanical read arms; the root parses no packet and no TCP state. The service polls (no wait set spans its three completion notifications and its client endpoints), as the driver and the existing service already do. Only four receive pages are in flight; a burst beyond that between polls is dropped by the device and reported by the driver's `stalled` count.

## Review surface

Start at `components/services/network-service/src/link.rs` (the device adapter and the release handshake) and `main.rs` (`attach_stack`, `release_stack`), then `contracts/network-interface/v1/schema.zt` and `boot-contracts/src/network_interface.rs`, then the tcp arm of `check-sel4-io-network-plane.py` with `scripts/lib/link_peer.py`. The closures and run records are generated.

Two design points worth a reader's eye: the link peer and buffer factory sit at compiled slots 0 and 1 because a loan's receiver is named by endpoint slot and the root reads that number as an endpoint only while no buffer occupies it; and request ids are odd on transmit, even on receive, because both queues charge one DMA account.

title: B93: the block driver answers shutdown only after its final drain
body:
## Claim

The block client's shutdown is now a rendezvous: `BlockIo::shutdown` is a `call` the driver answers only after its final drain, so a client cannot exit, and have its loans reclaimed, while `virtio-blk-driver` is still using the ring the client lent it. ## Change

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `components/lib/src/block_io.rs` | `shutdown` sends the same one byte as a `call` and returns on the driver's reply |
| `components/services/virtio-blk-driver/src/main.rs` | On `Shutdown`: drain, print `peer complete, exiting`, `reply`, then exit; the exit marker moved into that arm |
| `contracts/system-image-closure/v1/closures/`, `contracts/system-test-run/v1/runs/` | Regenerated for the changed component identities (`components/lib` is an input of every closure) |

title: H1V1 MAVLink lane: bench probe, board run, and the pad placed
body:
**Stacked on #26.** The first commit here is that PR's head; the nine after it are this lane's. GitHub will show the whole stack until #26 merges, after which this diff collapses to those nine.

## Change

Opens a lane to transmit a MAVLink v2 HEARTBEAT once per second from the resident Slime graph on the Novatek NT98690 H1V1, through the SoC's UART7 into an RFD900x telemetry radio, and lands its first session: a bench probe that answers the hardware questions from the vendor U-Boot prompt, and the board run that answered them.

- `scripts/lib/mavlink.py`: HEARTBEAT framing, the X.25 checksum, and a resynchronising v2 frame decoder, standard library only. The decoder consumes frames it cannot verify whole and resynchronises by one byte only on a failed checksum.
- `scripts/lib/uboot_console.py`: `Console.read_bytes_for`, factored out of `read_for`, so a framed binary protocol is read as bytes rather than through a lossy text decode.
- `scripts/check/check-nt98690-boot.py`: `--uart-probe` brings UART7 up from the prompt, transmits pinned heartbeats, and requires each to be decoded on a paired radio; `--uart-listen-seconds` checks the radio pair with no board attached; `--dry-run --uart-probe` renders the write list. Bench modes beside `--pwm-probe`: no marker contract, no `just` recipe, the gate count unchanged at 48.
- `sel4/pins.toml`, `scripts/check/check-sel4-pins.py`: UART7's addresses, clock arithmetic, and baud divisor pinned and bound to each other; the observed route, prompt-time words, and header position pinned from the board run and bound to the header map #26 carries.
- `scripts/check/check-nt98690-bench-probe.py`: a 16550 model, a ground-radio model that can spoil a frame three ways, and 25 further scenarios, 40 in all. Each new scenario was confirmed to fail against a reverted fix.
- `.tasks/items/`: the lane epic, the bench milestone (closed on the board run), an IO-track milestone for the board-neutral mechanism, and P6.E for the board gate.
- `devlog/`: the lane decision with its plan of record, and the probe's audit entry with both transcripts, the radio capture, and its decode.

## Claim

On the named H1V1, from its unmodified vendor U-Boot: UART7's clock, reset, mux, and pad words read their surveyed values before anything was written; the port took divisor 52 and 8N1 and read them back; ten heartbeats written to the transmit register a byte at a time were each decoded on the ground radio, the 210-byte capture byte-identical to the encoder's output for sequences 0 through 9; every shared word the probe changed was written back and read back; the vendor banner returned after `reset`.

The pad's position on the connector, header pin 13, rests on that run's wiring, an operator report, and on the frames having arrived through it. The meter reading the bench sheet asked for was not taken, and the entry, the item, the pins comment, and the checker's route table each say so.

This claims nothing about Slime. No Slime code transmits; the root's carve, the driver, the producer, and the one syscall the cadence needs are the lane's later sessions, and the middle one is board-neutral.

## Risk

PWM channel 12 drives this SoC's CPU core voltage, and its clock gate, divider, pad mux, and the reset shared by every PWM channel sit in the same clock-generator and pinmux pages this probe touches. UART7's words are disjoint from that set; every write is a read-modify-write of one field, every restoration is verified by readback, and the four core-rail readings are asserted before the first write and after the last. Nothing here runs under QEMU or in any gate, so the only regression surface is the pins checker's new assertions and the host model.

Two facts the plan had wrong were corrected by the board: the interrupt-identity register reports FIFO enable as `0x81`, not the datasheet's `0xC1`; and UART8, the first choice, has no data pins on this header at all, which is why the port is UART7.

## Review surface

`scripts/lib/mavlink.py` whole; `scripts/check/check-nt98690-boot.py` from `UART7_BASE` through `uart_probe`; the `uart7_*` keys in `sel4/pins.toml [ns02201_h1v1]` and their checks; `devlog/2026-09-10-h1v1-uart-probe/index.md` and its `## Investigation log`. `python3 scripts/check/check-nt98690-boot.py --dry-run --uart-probe` prints the exact write list the board run was held to.

body:
## Change

Opens a lane to drive a hobby drone ESC with servo PWM from the resident Slisp prompt on the
Novatek NT98690 H1V1, and lands its first session: bench modes that answer, from the vendor
U-Boot prompt, the hardware questions Slime's own bring-up would otherwise assume.

- `scripts/check/check-nt98690-boot.py`: `--gpio-probe` toggles one pad as a plain output slowly
  enough to find with a meter; `--pwm-probe` drives servo PWM on one channel and holds each pulse
  width long enough to watch a servo or ESC respond; `--dry-run` renders the write sequence with no
  board. Bench modes beside `--reset-probe`: no marker contract, no `just` recipe.
- `sel4/pins.toml`, `scripts/check/check-sel4-pins.py`: the PWM, pinmux, GPIO, and pad block
  bases, the clock arithmetic that makes one PWM count one microsecond, and seven facts observed on
  the board, all checked.
- `.tasks/items/`: the lane epic, the bench milestone (closed), an IO-track milestone for the
  board-neutral mechanism, and P6.D for the board evidence.
- `devlog/`: the lane decision with its plan of record, and the probe's audit entry with two raw
  transcripts.

## Claim

On the named H1V1: PWM0 reaches P_GPIO[0] on the 40-pin GPIO header; the block takes and reads back
the programmed clock, free-run, period, and extended-period values with channel 12 untouched; no
firmware in the boot path routes these channels (the pinmux word read zero and every P_GPIO was in
GPIO mode at handoff); the GPIO block does not report a pad held by another function; and a
complete run disables the channel, restores every shared word to its surveyed value, resets, and
returns the vendor banner. A drone ESC on the pad arming and changing speed is an operator
observation, recorded as such.

This claims nothing about Slime. No Slime code drives a pad; the root's carve, bring-up, driver,
and shell command are the lane's later sessions, and the middle one is board-neutral.

## Risk

PWM channel 12 drives this SoC's CPU core voltage, and its clock gate, divider, pad mux, and the
reset shared by every channel sit in the registers a servo channel needs. Three of those words are
never written; the rest are read-modify-write on one channel's bits; enable, disable, and load are
write-1-to-set; four core-rail readings are asserted before the first write and after the last.
Two full runs on the board left the rail intact. Nothing here runs under QEMU or in any gate, so
the only regression surface is the pins checker's new assertions.

title: feat(sel4/memory): scale private backing safely
body:
## Claim

Slime-root private-memory backing scales by live segmented ownership instead of per-task maximum-page arrays while preserving exact 4 KiB growth semantics and the aligned 2 MiB full-window path on AArch64 and RV64.

Capacity admission now describes the exact backing shape runtime provisioning retains. Consecutive one-page growth walks only the selected arena's reusable and in-flight records, not the root-wide allocation descriptor pool.

## Change

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Private frames | Adds architecture-qualified 2 MiB backing for an empty aligned 512-page private window, with exact base-page behavior elsewhere. |
| Task ownership | Replaces monolithic per-task arenas with one static extent plus bounded private-data and page-table extents backed by compact root-wide records. |
| Capacity accounting | Uses one clamped `PrivateBackingLayout` for supported runtime planning, admission, and provisioning, including the retained second 2 MiB data extent at quota 512. |
| Bounded traversal | Adds arena-local reusable-kind buckets and an in-flight chain while retaining compact owner/serial allocation records. |
| Direct allocation state | Carries lifetime-bound `PrivateAllocation` tokens through acquire, map, mark, reset, commit, and unwind without capability lookup scans. |
| Rollback boundary | Unwinds only records created by the failed transaction; mapped leaf tables and previously committed frames remain owned and mapped. |
| Failed-map ownership | Retains a retyped object whose mapping failed as an unmapped object of its own type, instead of declaring its CSlot empty while the kernel still holds the capability. |
| Cleanup | Guards private operations once arena release begins while preserving retryable cold owner/serial cleanup. |
| Host seam | Adds static `PrivateMemoryKernel` dispatch so host regressions execute the production growth body and record actual kernel requests. |
| Generated inputs | Refreshes all 52 system-image closures and makes the system-spec gate explicitly validate private-memory facts added after its immutable baseline. |

## Review map

| Start here | Why |
|---|---|
| `slime-root/src/object_allocator.rs` | Shared backing layout, compact allocation records, arena-local state lists, direct tokens, rollback, reclamation, and host regressions. |
| `slime-root/src/private_memory.rs` | Exact page growth, mixed 2 MiB/4 KiB backing, and kernel dispatch. |
| `slime-root/src/task.rs` | Pre-publication capacity reservation and live provisioning. |
| `slime-root/src/generation.rs` | Generation-wide root CSlot admission using the runtime allocation count. |
| `scripts/check/check-system-spec.py` | Checked post-baseline private-memory grants, bindings, notifications, and instance fields. |
| `scripts/check/check-sel4-private-memory-plane.py` | Runtime evidence for both QEMU architectures and injected failure cases. |

## Invariants

| Invariant | Enforcement |
|---|---|
| Public private memory remains exactly bounded at 512 pages. | Runtime layout clamps to the existing quota; planning above 512 remains hypothetical and does not expand runtime support. |
| Admission matches runtime provisioning. | Planning and live provisioning consume the same extent/request layout; quota 512 includes two 2 MiB data extents, 514 allocations, 4 extents, and 518 CSlots including the static anchor. |
| Incremental growth is arena-bounded. | Reusable acquisition and transaction completion follow validated per-arena links with a walk bound of `arena.slot_len`. |
| Stale state cannot cross task lifetimes. | Every token and linked record is checked against arena index, serial, owner, state, kind, slot, and release phase. |
| A failed growth affects only its own objects. | Rollback drains the in-flight chain only; committed records are not linked there. |
| Kernel and allocator agree about every live CSlot. | Retyped objects remain correctly typed when mapping fails and are reused without a second retype. |
| Task exit returns backing exactly once. | Release clears state heads before cold record deletion and preserves retryable serial-bound ownership until completion. |

## Verification

| Evidence | Result |
|---|---|
| `just test_sel4_root` | 227/227 passed across 19 modules. Includes exact provisioning traces, first-failure prefixes, capacity boundaries, two placement extremes, 512 one-page growths with exact visit counts, ownership corruption, release isolation, and real rollback/retry paths. |
| `just private_memory_check` | AArch64: 23 markers across 7 causal chains and 3 image cases. RV64: 23 markers across 7 causal chains and 1 image case. |
| `just sel4_root_boot_check` | Ordered generation, timer, task, IPC, fault, cleanup, and ready markers observed. |
| `just fmt_check_all` | Passed. |
| `just lint_all` | Passed with warnings denied. |
| `ruff check scripts/check/check-system-spec.py` | Passed. |
| `python3 scripts/check/check-system-spec.py` | 43 systems compiled and derived semantically identical to their committed fixtures; 21 named mutations refused. |
| `generate-system-image-closures.py --check` | All 52 closures current. |
| `just devlog_check` | 298 entries indexed and valid. |

## Latest review fixes

PR review against `9578922` identified two P2 defects:

1. The capacity planner described one 2 MiB data extent at quota 512 while runtime provisioning retained two. The shared layout now makes planning and provisioning identical for every supported quota.
2. Private acquisition and transaction operations searched the root-wide descriptor array. Arena-local reusable and in-flight chains now make consecutive small growth proportional to the selected arena's records.

The second data extent is intentional: it preserves small-page fallback after a failed large-frame map. The fix does not raise the runtime quota or claim a multi-span runtime policy above 512 pages.

## Known limits

- Public private memory remains capped at 512 pages; later memory-capacity work owns ceiling increases.
- The host recording kernel verifies control flow and requested primitives; real untyped allocation and mapping are established by the QEMU gates.
- Injected failure images remain AArch64-only; RV64 runs the normal private-memory plane.
- Physical RAM-map qualification remains separate; QEMU evidence is not board evidence.

title: Work-item store hard cutover: delete the pre-MyQue identifier system
body:
## Why

The MyQue migration landed structurally but left a compatibility layer that kept `roadmap/` a latent second authority over work-item identity: a 262-entry legacy id map, an ambiguity resolver for the twice-allocated `B29`/`B30`, and an importer able to rebuild `.tasks/items/` from roadmap headings. This finishes the cutover so `.tasks/items/<uuid>.md` is the only live authority and the migration is not permanent architecture.

Two review rounds then found five checker acceptance boundaries wrong. Each was reproduced against the committed code before being changed, and re-observed after.

## What changed

- **Devlog metadata is UUID-native.** All 288 pre-migration `| Roadmap | C7.4, B30 |` rows became `| Work items | <uuid>, <uuid> |`. The one ambiguous case (`B30` in `2026-08-07-b30-release-trust-gate`) resolved from the map's recorded `devlog_references` evidence, not by picking an allocation.
- **Compatibility deleted:** `.tasks/legacy-roadmap-ids.json` (307 lines), `scripts/migrate-roadmap-to-myque.py` (413), `scripts/lib/roadmap_inventory.py` (416), plus 92 lines of migration-only checker policy and 81 lines of legacy resolution. No roadmap-to-store reconstruction path remains.
- **`roadmap/00-backlog.md` frozen** as an index of pre-cutover anchors. The instruction to add a heading when closing an item is gone — a new defect is a `backlog`-tagged item plus a devlog entry, and no checker asks for more.
- **`roadmap/README.md` and `README.md` stopped mirroring state.** The hand-maintained `Current state` table (which had already drifted — 218 done against an actual 219) became a track ownership/boundary table; state strings were stripped from all 50 Mermaid nodes; the front page's per-track "M1–M4 complete / IO0–IO7 complete" list became a capability-and-evidence summary.
- **Review fixes:**
  - The frozen index no longer requires an indexed item to stay `done`/`cancelled`. Requiring it let a historical document veto a legitimate reopening in the canonical store. Whether a reopened defect blocks milestone work is `check_backlog_first()`'s question, and it answers it.
  - The index is parsed as heading-delimited **sections validated by position**, not as a set keyed by `B<N>`. The set form let the first `B29` mark the second `B29` verified — the same non-unique-key merge this cutover existed to remove.
  - Link `#fragment`s are validated instead of stripped. Anchor computation moved to `scripts/lib/markdown_anchors.py` with 11 executable controls `devlog_check` runs before trusting it: fences suppress headings, inline code keeps its literal text, duplicate headings take `-1`/`-2` suffixes, explicit anchors count.
  - Front matter is an exact field set. The old parser compared the first eight dict keys, so a trailing `Roadmap` row passed and a trailing duplicate `Work items | none` passed *while silently overriding the real UUID*.

## Invariants / risk

- **Frozen devlog bodies were not rewritten.** Only the front matter's machine fields changed. `devlog/README.md` and `AGENTS.md` now name a **Migratable** class for exactly that, because rewriting 288 landed entries contradicted the immutability rule as written. Prose is explicitly excluded — an entry may keep saying `roadmap/` was authoritative when it was written.
- **Inbound links preserved.** Auditing all 77 devlog fragment links found 4 broken since the day they were written (`#p549-and-c810`, `#p4--raspberry-pi-5-board-bring-up` match no heading in 20 revisions of `07-architecture-portability.md`). Restored with retained `<a id>` anchors rather than by editing frozen bodies.
- **MyQue still owns its schema.** No `work-item/v1` validation is reimplemented; `myque check` remains the authority for UUIDs, filenames, aliases, graph, cycles, and state consistency.
- **Keys survive as display aliases.** `devlog/README.md`'s index column was renamed `Roadmap` → `Keys` and kept as keys: 485 of those mentions name items whose keys are absent from the entry title, so UUID-ising it would destroy the only eye-scannable "which entry covers C8.14?" surface while protecting nothing.
- **Closure identity unaffected.** No declared release input changed; `just/` and `Justfile` are byte-identical.
- Known residue, recorded in the devlog entry: `roadmap/`'s 183 per-milestone `**Status:**` lines are scoped as frozen evidence but no gate enforces that reading; duplicate-heading anchors are positional, so an inserted section moves `#deliverables-7`; fragment validation covers links written inside devlog entries, not `roadmap/`↔`docs/` cross-links.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `just devlog_check` | pass — `291 entries, 291 indexed` |
| `just tasks_check` | pass — `274 items, 94 frozen backlog headings indexed` |
| `just ruff` | pass |
| `just typos` | pass |
| `generate-system-image-closures.py --check` | `50 system-image closures are current` |
| `markdown_anchors.controls()` | 11 cases, 0 failures |

Mutation-tested, 13 negative and 4 positive cases. The ones that changed behaviour in review:

| Mutation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Strip the **second** `B29`/`B30` section's `**Item:**` line | pass | fail — `B29 (heading 69 of 94) has no …Item…` |
| Link a heading present only inside a fenced example | pass | fail |
| Link `#tracks-1` with two `## Tracks` headings | fail | **pass** |
| Link the inline-code heading `` `release_trust_check` `` | fail | **pass** |
| Trailing extra `| Roadmap | C9.4 |` row | pass | fail |
| Trailing duplicate `| Work items | none |` row | pass (UUID silently lost) | fail |
| Delete every `### B<N>` entry | pass (`0 == 0`) | fail — fewer than the 94 that landed |
| Reopen an indexed item, no active milestone | fail (index vetoed) | **pass** |
| Reopen with `P5.4.2` active | fail ×4 | fail ×1, only `backlog-first: …` |

Unchanged and still failing correctly: a key instead of a UUID, an unknown UUID, `Roadmap` replacing `Work items`, a deleted referenced item, an index heading naming an absent item. Unchanged and still passing: a new `backlog` item present in no roadmap file, and rewording an unlinked heading.

Both anchor rules are load-bearing: regressing `slug()` to strip code spans as markup, or fence tracking to ignore fences, fails `devlog_check` with `anchor control:` findings before it reaches any entry.

title: Work-item identity: move from roadmap headings to a canonical MyQue store
body:
## Claim

Work-item identity is an immutable UUID in `.tasks/items/`, not the text of a
`roadmap/` Markdown heading. No checker derives identity from a heading, and
every one of the 837 work-item references across 288 merged devlog entries still
resolves — without rewriting a single merged entry.

## Change

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `.tasks/items/` | 272 canonical `work-item/v1` files under UUIDv7 filenames: 266 roadmap declarations, 5 keyless deferred follow-ups, and this migration's own item |
| `.tasks/legacy-roadmap-ids.json` | Committed map of 262 unique roadmap ids to UUIDs, plus both `B29`/`B30` collisions with source coordinates |
| `scripts/lib/roadmap_inventory.py` | One narrow reader of the legacy heading format: declarations, states, closure dates, parents, `**Depends on:**` prose. Used by the migration only |
| `scripts/migrate-roadmap-to-myque.py` | Deterministic, re-runnable import; allocates a UUIDv7 per declaration, backdated to the item's closure date |
| `scripts/lib/work_items.py` | Resolves a reference against `.tasks/items/` filenames; exposes the shallow fields policy checks need |
| `scripts/check/check-devlog.py` | Resolves references through the store. `ROADMAP_HEADING`, `ROADMAP_ID_DECLARATION`, `LEGACY_ROADMAP_ID_COLLISIONS`, `prove_roadmap_collision_guard`, `roadmap_ids`, and heading-derived `KNOWN_IDS` deleted — 148 lines net removed |
| `scripts/check/check-work-items.py` | `myque check`, then repository policy: backlog-first ordering, legacy-map integrity, undated-closure disclosure |
| `just/quality.just` | `tasks_check`, `tasks_list`, `tasks_next`, `tasks_graph` |
| `flake.nix` / `flake.lock` | `myque` input with `inputs.nixpkgs.follows`; `myque-bin` in the default shell |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | New `work_items` job with Nix quick-install and a flake-keyed store cache |
| `roadmap/`, `AGENTS.md`, `devlog/{README,TEMPLATE}.md` | Non-authoritative banners; identity, backlog, and front-matter guidance rewritten to name the canonical store |

## Review map

| Start here | Why |
|---|---|
| `devlog/2026-09-06-myque-work-item-identity/index.md` | The decisions, their rejected alternatives, and the mutation evidence behind every guard |
| `scripts/lib/work_items.py` | The resolution rule: the filename set *is* the identity set, per `work-item/v1` §3 |
| `scripts/check/check-devlog.py` | What the heading scraper was replaced by, and what was deleted rather than carried |
| `scripts/check/check-work-items.py` | Where MyQue's validity ends and Slime OS policy begins |
| `.tasks/legacy-roadmap-ids.json` | Why merged devlog front matter needed no rewrite |
| `scripts/migrate-roadmap-to-myque.py` | Determinism of the import; read only to re-audit the 272 items |

## Invariants

| Invariant | How preserved / enforced |
|---|---|
| Identity is a UUID; human keys are display-only | Keys are optional MyQue keys; no checker, dependency edge, or devlog reference resolves through one. The four colliding ids are deliberately keyless |
| A devlog reference always resolves to a real item | `just devlog_check` resolves against `.tasks/items/`, falling back to the committed legacy map |
| An ambiguous legacy id fails closed | `B29`/`B30` were each allocated twice; an entry naming one with no recorded resolution fails rather than picking an allocation |
| The legacy map cannot drift from the store | `just tasks_check` rejects a mapped UUID absent from `.tasks/items/` |
| A closure date is an observed fact | 34 items whose date is unrecoverable carry the migration date *and say so*; `just tasks_check` enforces the disclosure, scoped to imported items so a genuine same-day closure is not forced to lie |
| Merged devlog entries are never rewritten | `git diff --stat devlog/` after the checker rewrite is empty |
| `devlog_check` stays binary-free | It reads filenames instead of shelling out to `myque`, so `docs_gates` remains a checkout-plus-`just` job |

## Verification

| Evidence | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| `just tasks_check` → `work-item check passed: 272 items, 262 legacy ids mapped` | Store validates under `myque check` and repository policy |
| `just devlog_check` → `devlog check passed: 289 entries, 289 indexed` | All references resolve without heading parsing |
| `just ruff` → `All checks passed!` | Python lint over the new scripts |
| `just typos` → clean | Spell-check survives 272 UUID-named files |
| Mutation: unresolvable reference `Z99` | Fails with the unresolvable-reference message |
| Mutation: `B30` in an entry with no recorded resolution | Fails closed, naming the ambiguity |
| Mutation: legacy map pointed at a non-existent UUID | Fails with the drift message |
| Mutation: undated-closure disclosure stripped from one item | Fails with the disclosure message |
| Dependency cycle `P3 → P3.E → P3` | Caught by `myque check` on the first import; fixed at the source, not suppressed |
| `nix develop --command myque check` on locked `db1c81f` | Store does not depend on unpublished CLI fixes |
| `myque list --state <s>` across six states | 218 done, 42 deferred, 8 cancelled, 3 blocked, 1 active, 0 open — 272 total |

No runtime tests were run: this change touches no guest code, no contract, and
no Rust crate. Every Rust and QEMU gate is untouched.

## Known limits

- `flake.lock` pins myque `db1c81f`, which predates the store-relative
  abbreviation fix; `myque list` prints one repeated token for the nine keyless
  items. `myque check` is unaffected. Update once the fix is published.
- `myque-bin` has no published binary cache, so a cold `work_items` run builds
  it through GHC (117 paths, 516 MiB fetched). The job is cached on `flake.lock`.
- 50 devlog links carry `roadmap/` heading anchors. They resolve because the
  item sections were kept, but `check-devlog.py` validates the file, not the
  anchor.
- `roadmap/README.md`'s track table says "CP11–CP15 planned" while each declares
  Complete in its own section. The summary is stale, not the items; left as
  found, because reconciling a track narrative is a separate change.
- 5 items (`C8.13.1`, `C8.13.2`, `P3.D`, `IO2`, `IO4`) are `done` with named
  unfinished residue, faithfully reproducing the roadmap's narrowed exit
  conditions. Consumers must read the exit condition, not the state alone.
- `devlog/README.md` is still a central index every entry appends to, so
  branch-concurrent devlog entries conflict even though work items no longer do.

## Evidence / history

title: P6: bring up Slime OS on the Novatek NT98690 H1V1
body:
## P6: bring up Slime OS on the Novatek NT98690 H1V1

**Change.** The whole P6 lane, purely additive over #20: firmware-handoff probe and gate (P6.A), seL4 and slime-root on the board with a watchdog reset and byte-identical repeated boots (P6.B), and a resident Slisp session over the product UART (P6.C). Concretely: target profile 8 `aarch64-sel4-nt98690-h1v1`; the `ns02201-h1v1` seL4 platform and prefix; a bare-metal probe payload under `tools/nt98690/`; a payload builder that wraps the kernel loader in the arm64 `Image` header the probe qualified; a U-Boot console driver; three checkers with `just nt98690_{boot,sel4,slisp}_check`; the root's NT98690 watchdog reset; four devlog entries with raw transcripts; roadmap P6 blocks; and `DEMO.md`.

**Prerequisite.** The pins name one commit in each fork that is not yet on `iceice666`: `1b93edf5` in seL4 ("feat(ns02201): add the Novatek NT98690 H1V1 platform") and `20905bef` in rust-sel4 ("feat(kernel-loader): add an ns02201 platform"). Both are on `CG-AA/{seL4,rust-sel4}` branch `slime-ns02201-h1v1`. This tree keeps `.gitmodules` and `sel4/pins.toml` on the iceice666 forks; cherry-pick those two commits there (or tell me the SHAs you land them at and I re-pin). A fork commit that adds a platform moves every platform's generated kernel config hash, so `sel4/pins.toml` re-pins those hashes for all platforms; every other pinned artifact is byte-identical.

title: x86-64 seL4 bring-up: GRUB Multiboot2 boot, native root execution, and the product graph under QEMU
body:
## Claim

Pinned QEMU q35/OVMF boots upstream seL4 and the x86-64 `slime-root` through one
GRUB Multiboot2 EFI tree; the root's native task/IPC/fault/timer/reclamation
slice runs to `SLIME_ROOT READY`; and the resident
`init`/`console`/`spawn-service`/Slisp graph evaluates an expression typed into
live COM1 input and spawns `sysinfo` through its declared context endpoint.

That is a **QEMU** claim. This PR is a draft because P6's physical evidence —
P6.5's deterministic removable image and P6.6's Framework boot — has not been
measured. Nothing here should be read as a hardware result.

Closes P6.2, P6.3, P6.4. P6.1 (`e08cb36`) and the planning entry (`12089c5`)
are on this branch as context and were reviewed previously.

## Change

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `sel4/config/qemu-pc99.cmake` | Three settings diverge from the inherited X64 **proof** profile, each pinned beside the emulator fact forcing it: `KernelSupportPCID` off, `KernelMaxNumBootinfoUntypedCaps` and `KernelRootCNodeSizeBits` back to seL4's own defaults |
| `sel4/pins.toml`, `flake.nix` | `[qemu_pc99_boot]` pins OVMF and EFI-format GRUB by store path, with an order-sensitive digest over the module list linked into `BOOTX64.EFI`; `[qemu_pc99]` gains the CPU-feature and boot-file contract |
| `deps/rust-sel4` | Fork `main` merged and repinned: x86-64 entry stack alignment, plus the `IOPort` cap type and 8-bit accessors seL4 defines invocations for but the safe wrapper never exposed |
| `scripts/lib/pc99_media.py` | Assembles and digests the EFI tree; verifies pinned firmware and module bytes before writing anything |
| `scripts/lib/sel4_boot.py` | One platform-aware identity check and boot path shared by every plane gate, replacing four near-copies |
| `slime-root/src/thread_abi.rs` | Owns the entry stack pointer for every thread the root starts directly |
| `slime-root/src/platform_timer.rs` | HPET status cleared between arming and enabling; interrupt routed off the pin the 8254 shares |
| `slime-root/src/device.rs`, `console.rs` | COM1 16550 receiver over an I/O-port capability; the console dispatcher's IPC buffer named through `next_event` |

## Review map

| Start here | Why |
|---|---|
| `sel4/config/qemu-pc99.cmake` | The three inherited-profile divergences. Each is a real weakening of a *proof* configuration — judge whether the stated justification holds |
| `slime-root/src/thread_abi.rs` | The SysV entry-alignment rule and its two callers. Small, load-bearing, and the fix for two separate `#GP` faults |
| `slime-root/src/platform_timer.rs:62-92` | Why the HPET moved off IOAPIC pin 2, and the clear-then-enable ordering |
| `scripts/lib/pc99_media.py` | What a boot claim binds to: the tree digest, the firmware pins, the module-order digest |
| `scripts/check/check-sel4-pins.py` | The gate that makes those pins observations rather than notes |

## Invariants

| Invariant | How preserved / enforced |
|---|---|
| A boot reads only bytes the identity manifest describes | Path-sensitive tree digest plus per-file digests, recomputed by the gate before QEMU starts |
| The firmware, bootloader, and module set are exactly the pinned ones | `check-sel4-pins.py` recomputes firmware hashes and the order-sensitive module digest; verified to fail closed on a module reorder |
| The kernel configuration cannot drift back toward the proof profile | Exact override table in the pin gate |
| The emulator still provides what the profile depends on | The pin gate launches the pinned machine and reads TCG's refusal set, so `cpu_features` and `qemu_features_unavailable` describe an observed accelerator |
| W^X stays enforced where the architecture can express it | Per-platform `WX_PROBES`; x86-64 records `wx_execute=unenforced` and drops the probe rather than passing it vacuously |
| Boot media stays reproducible | Two normalized builds compared across boot media and GRUB config |
| AArch64 and RV64 evidence is untouched | 31 AArch64 boot-layout fixtures unchanged; x86-64 fixtures recorded under their own directory |

## Verification

| Evidence | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| `just x86_64_sel4_root_boot_check` | P6.2 + P6.3 — the ordered marker chain exists only if the GRUB layout booted *and* the native root arms behaved |
| `just x86_64_qemu_check` | P6.4 — root boot, wait-set, sample, product graph, 3 boot layouts, portability |
| `just x86_64_sel4_image_check` | Two normalized builds byte-identical across boot media, GRUB config, kernel, root, child, component, generation, identity |
| `just sel4_pin_check` | Firmware, bootloader, module digest, kernel-config overrides, and the accelerator's feature set |
| `just test`, `just sel4_boot_layout_check` | No AArch64 regression; 31 layouts unchanged |
| `just lint_all`, `fmt_check_all`, `ruff`, `typos`, `test_host`, `contracts_check`, `architecture_contract_check` | pass |
| `cargo test -p slime-root --lib` | 217 passed |

Five defects were root-caused to reach the boot; each is a distinct mechanism,
not a retry:

1. `PCIDs not supported` — the proof profile requires PCID/INVPCID; TCG
   implements neither on any model.
2. `user exception 0xd` at the root's first `movaps` — upstream `stack_init`
   over-corrects by 8 once the x86-64 arm reaches Rust through a second `call`.
3. `NoKernelUntyped` → `DeviceTableFull` → `SlotRangeTooLarge` — q35 declares
   more untypeds and a larger root CNode than the proof profile and the root's
   own tables allowed.
4. Unbounded `SLIME_CLOCK expired due=0` — the HPET shared IOAPIC pin 2 with the
   still-enabled 8254, *and* enabling delivery over a latched status
   re-asserted immediately.
5. `user exception 0xd` in the console dispatcher — the same ABI mismatch as (2)
   in a second thread-start site.

## Known limits

- **No physical evidence.** P6.5 and P6.6 are unstarted. No Framework has booted
  this, no removable image exists, and no claim here extends past QEMU.
- The x86-64 boot-layout corpus covers 3 planes against AArch64's 31; the rest
  build only for platforms later milestones own.
- The generation, rollback, and capability-layout planes are not replayed on
  x86-64 — their generations need a storage transport this milestone does not own.
- The HPET frequency is the pinned 10 MHz emulator fact, not read from the
  capability register. H1 owns real inventory.
- `just test_sel4_root` cannot run in this environment for a reason predating
  this branch: it builds `sel4-sys` for the host against the AArch64 prefix and
  host clang rejects that prefix's inline asm. The same 217 tests were run
  directly against the pc99 prefix.
- DMA remains trusted; no IOMMU containment is claimed.

## Evidence / history

- Devlog: [`devlog/2026-09-03-p6-2-p6-4-x86-64-boot/`](../blob/roadmap/amd64-sel4-bringup/devlog/2026-09-03-p6-2-p6-4-x86-64-boot/index.md), with the first full root-boot serial capture
- Devlog: [`devlog/2026-09-02-p6-1-x86-64-sel4-target/`](../blob/roadmap/amd64-sel4-bringup/devlog/2026-09-02-p6-1-x86-64-sel4-target/index.md) (P6.1)
- Roadmap: [P6.2/P6.3/P6.4](../blob/roadmap/amd64-sel4-bringup/roadmap/07-architecture-portability.md), all marked complete with observed exit conditions and gates
- Fork: `iceice666/rust-sel4@14d98403` — the platform work merged to that fork's `main`

title: Milk-V Duo physical lane: RV64 seL4, board qualification, and the resident Slisp shell
body:
## Claim

A named Milk-V Duo physically boots upstream seL4 and `slime-root`, admits only a target-qualified `riscv64-sel4-milkv-duo` generation, and runs the resident product graph with Slisp as an interactive shell driven over the board's own UART0 — with repeatable normalized evidence, zero framing errors, and autonomous recovery to vendor Linux after every boot. RV64 QEMU is established first as the architecture-neutral reference the physical lane consumes.

This is not a product-equivalence claim. Raspberry Pi 5 and Framework keep their own board and peripheral gates, and neither can be closed from Duo evidence. Storage, USB, network, display, sensor, and actuator qualification remain out of scope.

## Change

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `sel4/pins.toml`, `sel4/config/cv1800b-duo.cmake` | Pin the CV1800B board from values read off the running board and vendor firmware: DRAM window, OpenSBI reservation, the 25 MHz timebase, and the `riscv,plic0` layout. QEMU's 10 MHz timer is wrong for this SoC and OpenSBI 0.9 implements no SRST, so both are pinned facts |
| `sel4/config/qemu-riscv-virt.cmake`, `scripts/build/build-sel4.py` | RV64 QEMU profile: upstream seL4 plus a target-qualified root and component path |
| `tools/duo/payload/`, `scripts/build/build-duo-payload.py` | Flat payload wrapped in a FIT, because vendor U-Boot 2021.10 compiles in neither `go`, `booti`, nor `bootelf`. The build cross-checks linker base, ELF entry, and pinned load address so a mislinked payload fails at build rather than hanging on the board |
| `slime-root/src/{main,platform_timer,object_allocator,device,fault,child_vspace}.rs` | RV64/AArch64 boundaries for timer, device mapping, ELF, component entry, and loader detail; C906 MAEE page-table encoding; physical RTC/PLIC path |
| `slime-root/src/{console,device}.rs`, `graph_runtime/` | Map the board's DW APB UART0 receive page read-only, consume line-status errors without forwarding corrupted bytes, and serve bytes through Slisp's existing `InputRead` grant. Slisp receives no MMIO or device capability |
| `scripts/check/check-duo-{boot,sel4,slisp,gate-control}.py` | Physical gates that fail closed: a missing board, link, adapter, marker, or out-of-order marker each exits nonzero, and no QEMU pass substitutes |
| `scripts/check/*plane*.py`, `scripts/lib/harness.py` | Cross-platform plane checkers so the architecture-neutral corpus replays on both profiles |
| `roadmap/`, `devlog/` | P3, P3.D, P3.E, P3.F recorded with their evidence, including the two defects the physical campaigns exposed |

## Review map

| Start here | Why |
|---|---|
| `devlog/2026-08-31-p3e-sel4-milkv-duo/index.md` | The campaign narrative: what was observed, in what order, and which two defects the board exposed that QEMU could not |
| `sel4/pins.toml` | Every board fact this lane rests on; the provenance of each value is stated in `9001bc9`'s message |
| `slime-root/src/platform_timer.rs` | Largest behavioral surface (+352); RTC/PLIC and the stopped-counter fix |
| `slime-root/src/object_allocator.rs` | +216; the fragmented-slot fixture the AArch64 host tests forced a correction to |
| `scripts/check/check-duo-sel4.py` | What the physical claim actually asserts, and what makes it fail |
| `devlog/2026-08-31-p3e-loader-ad-bits/`, `devlog/2026-09-01-p3e-rtc-counter-start/` | The two root-caused defects, each with its raw capture |

## Invariants

| Invariant | How preserved / enforced |
|---|---|
| A component receives no ambient device authority | Slisp gets bytes through its declared `InputRead` grant; the UART0 receive page is mapped read-only in `slime-root` and no MMIO or device capability is delegated |
| Only target-qualified images are admitted | The generated target-profile contract is checked before executable mapping; the Duo generation is `riscv64-sel4-milkv-duo` and QEMU's is distinct |
| Physical evidence is never substituted by QEMU | `duo_*_check` are physical and fail closed; `duo_gate_control_check` mutates the committed transcript one way at a time and requires all 27 mutations to fail, so the marker chain is load-bearing rather than decorative |
| The board is recoverable without physical intervention | The payload returns into U-Boot rather than calling SBI SHUTDOWN, which this firmware's OpenSBI 0.9 does not implement; stock `boot.sd` is untouched so autoboot is the recovery path |
| Architecture-specific detail stays behind explicit boundaries | RV64/AArch64 splits in timer, device, ELF, entry, and loader paths rather than conditionals spread through mechanism |

## Verification

| Evidence | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| `just duo_sel4_check <serial>` | Passed on the named board: three physical sample boots with byte-identical normalized semantic traces, zero framing errors, a bounded early-fault diagnostic, and cold reset to vendor Linux after all four boots |
| `just duo_slisp_check <serial>` | Passed on the named board: three UART0 commands through Slisp's `InputRead` authority, state retained, `sysinfo` launched through its declared spawn profile, bounded return to vendor Linux |
| `just duo_boot_check <serial>` | Observed `sxstatus=0x0000000040638000`, decoded `MAEE=1`, payload completion and vendor recovery |
| `just duo_gate_control_check` | The observed transcript passes and all 27 missing/reordered/explicit-failure mutations are rejected |
| `just riscv64_qemu_check` | The RV64 QEMU reference corpus — root, wait/wake, sample, generation, rollback |
| `just slisp_core_check`, `just sel4_component_graph_check` | Slisp and the resident graph under QEMU |
| `slime-root` host tests under `qemu-aarch64` | 214/214 against the pinned AArch64 prefix; the first run caught the new fragmented-slot fixture |
| `just fmt_check_all`, `just lint_all`, `just devlog_check` | Repository hygiene |

## Known limits

- Two roadmap statements are stale and contradict the P3.F section this branch marks complete. `roadmap/07-architecture-portability.md:5` still calls P3.F "an open product-shell follow-up", and `roadmap/README.md:20` still calls it "the next Duo follow-up", while `roadmap/07-architecture-portability.md:324` says "Complete and physically verified 2026-09-01". The section is authoritative; both summaries need updating. Left for the author rather than edited here.
- P3.E and P3.F are single-board claims. One named Milk-V Duo, one serial adapter, one vendor firmware version.
- P4 (Raspberry Pi 5) board boot stays deferred: the available USB-UART adapter produces no bytes and the debug header is this image's only console. Unchanged by this branch.
- The physical gates require the board and adapter attached; CI cannot run them, so their evidence is the recorded campaigns rather than a pipeline result.
