## Why

Publishing the component SDK was already a workflow, but three of its preconditions were operator discipline rather than mechanism. CP7's deliverable requires publishing "only from an exact **protected** `slime_os` commit **after CP6 and the existing external-component gates pass**", and neither clause was implemented; CP9 makes the change classification computable but nothing computed it before a publication was attempted.

## What changed

- New `guard` job: refuses a dispatch ref other than `refs/heads/main`, then separately refuses a `github.sha` that `git merge-base --is-ancestor` does not place on `origin/main`. `fetch-depth: 0` so ancestry is decidable.
- `publish` names `needs: [guard, build-prefixes]` and re-asserts the ref in its own `if`, so a later dependency edit cannot silently reopen publication from an arbitrary branch.
- `component_sdk_export_check` and `component_sdk_release_check` now run before the credentialed job. Timeout 30 → 90 to cover them.
- New `scripts/check/check-component-sdk-preflight.py` and `just component_sdk_preflight`: clones the hosted release, exports the current commit, and reports the classification, the moved axes, and the lowest admissible version. `--require-version` turns it into the gate the workflow uses on the operator's input.

## Invariants / risk

- A recorded `sourceCommit` is now reachable from `main`, which is what makes CP7's reverse-drift check able to regenerate a release from the commit it names.
- Ref name and commit containment are checked independently: they fail differently, and only containment is the property reverse drift needs.
- The preflight compares the profile axis over the intersection of hosted and exported profiles and prints `NOT COMPARED` for the rest. Treating an absent profile as `profiles:removed` would manufacture a breaking change out of how the gate was invoked; ignoring it silently would overclaim.
- The preflight overstates nothing and writes nothing; it reaches no release credential.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `just component_sdk_preflight --profile aarch64-sel4-qemu-virt` | pass; hosted `2.0.0` (source `e6e1a91`) vs `ce256d2` → `breaking`, required `3.0.0`, naming `syscallAbi`, `contractSet`, `crates:changed:…`, `profiles:changed:aarch64-sel4-qemu-virt` |
| `--require-version 3.0.0` / `2.1.0` / `2.0.1` | exit 0 / 1 / 1; refusals name the required version |
| `guard` shell logic against real refs | 3 arms: main+main passes; feature ref refused; main ref carrying an off-main commit refused |
| Workflow YAML parse and job graph | pass; `guard` → `build-prefixes` → `publish` |
| `just devlog_check` | pass; 268 entries, 268 indexed |
| `just ruff`, `just typos`, `just --list` | pass |
| `component_sdk_export_check`, `component_sdk_release_check` | **not run locally**; both boot QEMU and publish to a stand-in repository. Wired in, unobserved in this session |

## Related

- [CP7, CP9](roadmap/10-component-platform.md)
- Devlog: [`devlog/2026-09-01-sdk-publication-guards/`](devlog/2026-09-01-sdk-publication-guards/index.md)
- Predecessor: [`devlog/2026-08-26-cp7-hosted-publication-hardening/`](devlog/2026-08-26-cp7-hosted-publication-hardening/index.md)
- Follow-up left open: hosted `sdk-v2.0.0` still has no compatibility-matrix row, and no `component_sdk_*` gate runs in `ci.yml`

title: chore(repo/hygiene): consolidate verification ownership
body:
## Claim

Repository artifacts now have explicit ownership boundaries: contracts and docs own system meaning, checker implementations own verification semantics, devlogs own investigation and evidence, and Justfiles own command orchestration and dependency order.

Four materially different seL4 I/O plane gates share one image-identity and QEMU process runtime without merging their independent verification claims. The standing gate-control checker now permanently proves both marker contracts and the shared identity/process runtime fail closed.

## Change

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| PR workflow | Add concise ordinary-change and system-change templates. |
| Repository guidance | Define comment, PR, devlog, checker, and Justfile ownership. Devlog entries correspond to logical events rather than commits. |
| Contract verification | Move slot-pin validation under the existing contract checker while preserving `just contracts_check`. |
| Just orchestration | Remove duplicated roadmap, checker, marker, scenario, and investigation prose from `just/*.just`. |
| Compatibility | Keep legacy recipes as a concise alias registry; unavailable physical gates still fail closed. |
| Zutai models | Consolidate four repeated model-check command pairs behind private `_zutai_model path` orchestration. |
| seL4 plane runtime | Add `scripts/lib/sel4_plane.py` for image identity, pinned QEMU command construction, bounded transcript capture, terminal stopping, and terminate/wait/kill cleanup. |
| Pilot migration | Move network, queue, block, and driver-authority gates to the shared runtime while retaining local fixtures, marker chains, failure markers, device arguments, and semantic postconditions. |
| Permanent controls | Extend `check-sel4-gate-controls.py` to call the shipped identity and runtime helpers through temporary files, a controlled `PATH`, minimal pins, and a fake QEMU executable. |
| Comment discipline | Replace roadmap, backlog, review, and migration chronology around pinned marker counts with current invariants. |

## Review map

| Start here | Why |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Artifact ownership and logical-event devlog lifecycle. |
| `scripts/check/check-sel4-gate-controls.py` | Existing marker mutations plus permanent identity and fake-QEMU runtime controls. |
| `scripts/lib/sel4_plane.py` | Shared seL4 image and QEMU process mechanism; unchanged in the close-out commit. |
| `scripts/lib/sel4_gate_markers.py` | Unchanged owner of marker-contract semantics. |
| `scripts/check/check-sel4-io-{network,queue,block,driver-authority}-plane.py` | Thin pilot gates with case-specific claims left local. |
| `scripts/check/check-contracts.py` | Slot-pin validation moved into its owning contract checker. |
| `scripts/check/contracts/slot_pin_reasons.py` | Current slot-pin invariant implementation. |
| `just/contracts.just` | Parameterized Zutai model-check orchestration and stable public recipes. |
| `just/compatibility.just` | Legacy alias registry and fail-closed unavailable hardware gates. |
| `devlog/2026-08-30-repository-hygiene/index.md` | Consolidated decisions, measurements, controls, and verification for all hygiene rounds. |

## Invariants and risk

- Root `Justfile` remains imports plus navigation.
- All 187 public recipe names remain present in identical order.
- Existing recipe dependencies and executable commands remain unchanged except exact Zutai command deduplication.
- `sel4_gate_markers.py` remains the sole owner of ordered evidence and failure-marker semantics.
- `sel4_plane.py` remains the sole owner of image identity and QEMU process semantics.
- Missing images/manifests, malformed or invalid identities, missing QEMU, timeout, and early process failure make `sel4_gate_control_check` red.
- IO2 writable/read-only disk arguments and backing-disk byte verification remain local and unchanged.
- The I/O link gate remains local because its UDP echo thread and socket cleanup do not justify a generic lifecycle hook.
- No new top-level checker executable was introduced.
- No additional plane checker was migrated in the close-out round. Remaining migrations are opportunistic only when substantive work touches a gate.
- Physical Framework and NVMe compatibility gates continue to fail closed.

## Measurement

Five I/O gates were inspected. Before the pilot they contained five image-identity implementations and five QEMU lifecycle implementations. Four pilot gates migrated; those four entrypoints now contain zero copies of either mechanism. The unselected I/O link gate retains one independent lifecycle.

The permanent gate control exercises 45 protected gates, 1,748 marker/layout mutations, eight identity cases, and four runtime cases without real QEMU.

## Verification

| Command/scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `just contracts_check` | Passed. |
| `just io_network_check` | Passed. |
| `just io_queue_check` | Passed. |
| `just io_block_check` | Passed, including backing-disk byte verification. |
| `just io_driver_authority_check` | Passed, including automatic binding-slot assertions. |
| `just sel4_gate_control_check` | Passed 1 valid and 7 invalid identity cases; terminal completion, timeout cleanup, early nonzero exit, and missing QEMU; plus all 1,748 marker/layout mutations. |
| `just devlog_check` | Passed: 267 entries indexed. |
| `just ruff` | Passed. |
| `just typos` | Passed. |
| `just fmt_check_all` | Passed. |
| `just --list` and `just --fmt --check` | Passed across all imported Justfiles. |
| Public `just --summary` comparison | Identical 187 recipe names in identical order. |
| Zutai model recipes, `just --dry-run` | Original build command and exact four model paths preserved. |
| `git diff --check` | Passed. |

The four pilot public gates were not rerun for the close-out commit because neither `sel4_plane.py` nor the pilot checkers changed. Their observed post-migration results above remain the runtime evidence. Full PR CI is the remaining merge gate.

title: Slot pin reasons: every pinned capability slot states a checkable why
body:
Closes **B91**. Every pinned capability slot in every generation manifest now states *why* it is pinned, in a form the builder measures rather than trusts — and the backlog reaches zero open items.

The load-bearing rule is **a pin is a claim, and a claim is checkable**. 616 of 679 instance binding slots were explicitly pinned with nothing distinguishing a number a boot-layout fixture freezes, a number a neighbouring binding's allocation depends on, a number the encoded layout would change without, and a number that is simply left over. No gate could tell a load-bearing pin from noise; the only way to find out was to delete one and boot.

> **Three vocabularies were proposed and two were disproved by measurement, not review.** The first partition's `allocatorOrder` label was false for **185 of its 196 members**. Its correction pushed those 185 into a class they could not honestly join. Both dead ends are recorded rather than hidden — see [Why four labels](#why-four-labels-and-not-three). A later pass then refuted two of its own follow-up gates the same way: [Two refuted gates](#two-refuted-gates).

## What lands

| Slice | What it adds | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| Inference cutover | 13 redundant pins removed from 4 compositions; each owning plane gate asserts the slot stays omitted *and* resolves to its frozen value | `sel4_demo_check`, `sel4_component_graph_check`, `sel4_loan_check`, `io_driver_authority_check` |
| `slotReason` | `InstanceBinding.slotReason` and `SlotPin.reason`, required exactly when `slot` is present, closed to four values | `contracts_check` |
| Builder validation | `pin_removal_effects` measures every pin through the production allocator; `validate_slot_reasons` refuses any label it cannot confirm, before `assign_declared_slots` | every product build |
| Repo-wide gate | `check-slot-pin-reasons.py`: totality, soundness, and a minimality clause auditing `componentAbi` against Rust **and** C sources | `contracts_check` |
| Spec propagation | `SlotPin.reason` required in `system-spec/v1` and propagated into derived bindings; `slotReason` treated as a post-baseline field | `system_spec_check` |
| Migration regression | `MIGRATED_PINS` asserts each of the five deleted pins stays unpinned *and* still resolves to the slot the allocator produced | `contracts_check` |

## The four labels

Ordered strongest first; the builder assigns the strongest effect that holds over the source manifest **and every boot profile built from it**.

| Label | Means | Count |
|---|---|---|
| `bootLayout` | The binding produces a `contracts/boot-layout/v1` row | 152 |
| `allocatorOrder` | Removing it moves *another* binding's slot | 12 |
| `encodedLayout` | Removing it moves only this binding's own encoded slot | 187 |
| `componentAbi` | Nothing moves — only component source can justify the number | 260 |

**611 pins across 43 manifests and 4 boot profiles**, plus 2 pins on a sourceless executable (`dango`) reported as exempt rather than silently skipped.

Profile awareness is not decoration: `resolve_boot_profile` filters bindings, so a label true of the whole composition can be false of what actually boots. `valid.zti#default` forces two `powerbox-chooser` pins from `componentAbi` to `encodedLayout`.

## Why four labels, and not three

The first vocabulary was `bootLayout` / `allocatorOrder` / `componentAbi`, and it passed its own gate. It was wrong.

`redundant_pin_bindings` compared the whole resolved table **including the pin's own entry**, so "removing this pin moves something" was true whenever the pin moved *itself*. That is every pin whose number differs from the allocator's choice — a tautology, not a property. **185 of 196 `allocatorOrder` pins moved nothing but themselves**, and the label exempted them from the one clause that could have questioned them.

Excluding the pin's own entry pushed all 185 into `componentAbi` — a class asserting *component source consumes this position*. Joint-removal testing showed none of them were removable: the encoded layout changes. So the honest partition needs a fourth class for "the number is load-bearing, but the manifest itself is what bears it", which is `encodedLayout`.

An independent reviewer built a classification oracle over all 43 manifests and reported **0 mismatches** against each pin's measured removal effect.

## Five pins deleted

Every pin the gate can prove both redundant *and* name-resolved is gone:

- `spawn-service/spawn-service-echo`, `spawn-service/spawn-service-sysinfo` (via `system-spec/v1/systems/reference.zti`)
- `io-link-loopback/network-service-link-device`, `network-service/network-intruder-service`, `network-service/network-service-link-device` (`sel4-io-network.zti`)

Two were found only after the clause learned to see `resolve_binding` through a one-argument wrapper — sixteen crates define one, and a name test blind to it reads those grants as positional.

**Nothing observable changed.** All **1084 resolved slots** across the corpus are byte-identical before and after (SHA-256 `95e360e7…`), and `generation.bin` is byte-identical for both compositions that lost a pin (`sel4-loan` `48501549…`, `sel4-io-network` `557179d5…`).

## Two refuted gates

Three follow-ups were classified as cheap gate work. Measuring each before building it refuted two.

**Code-path scoping is wrong, not merely imprecise.** The minimality clause matches a pinned number anywhere in the holder's sources, so one executable's two branches can cover for each other. Scoping the two claims to a single function was implemented — and flagged `io-driver-worker`'s four pins, *all of which are load-bearing*:

```
worker declared      : {probe-device: 0, probe-mmio: 1, probe-irq: 2, probe-dma: 3}
worker after removal : {probe-device: 0, probe-mmio: 3, probe-irq: 2, probe-dma: 1}
run_driver compiles  : DEVICE_SLOT=0 REGION_SLOT=1 IRQ_SLOT=2 DMA_SLOT=3
```

`run_supervisor` resolves those four names and forwards them **in array order** to `spawn` — which is precisely *how* they become the worker's positional slots. Splitting name-resolution from positional use across functions is the correct shape, so the crate-wide predicate is the one that survives it. Reverted; a real tightening needs the grant's ordinal in the `spawn` array, not its enclosing function.

**A permutation gate is unnecessary.** No host gate checks *which* number a pin carries. The prior entry asserted QEMU catches a permutation; this branch installed one and confirmed it rather than inheriting the claim — pin-reason gate and `check-boot-layout-resource.py` both green, `just io_driver_authority_check` fails with `[io-driver-probe] fail: `. The obvious host substitute, joint-removal equality, was also tested and **does not hold on the clean tree either**: the allocator refills freed pins lowest-first and reorders the group. A name-to-constant heuristic was tested too and has false positives on known-good source.

## Gate teeth

The gate is checked for teeth rather than assumed to have them. Nine mutation controls fail closed: a missing label, three wrong-label variants, an unknown value, a label on an unpinned binding, `allocatorOrder`→`encodedLayout` on a real pin, a re-pinned migrated binding, and a renamed migrated grant. `check-system-spec.py` gained one control, taking it from 20 to 21 refused mutations — and its Justfile comment claiming 17 is corrected to the observed count.

Two deliberate fail-closed paths: an executable whose sources cannot be read **fails** rather than defaulting to empty evidence (which made the clause vacuous for exactly the components it could not parse), and every `MIGRATED_PINS` entry must be reached, so a rename cannot silently retire its own assertion.

## Honest limits

The minimality clause reaches **4 of 260** `componentAbi` pins: 2 are exempt as sourceless, and 254 are held by components that never resolve that grant by name, where it has nothing to object to. It is a tripwire for pins that *become* migratable — not evidence the other 254 were audited. This is stated in the module docstring and the devlog, because a green run would otherwise imply an audit that did not happen.

Also unaddressed, and recorded: 187 `encodedLayout` pins are unexamined per composition; 11 compositions have no `.layout` fixture; minted (83) and notification (322) bindings remain fully explicit and carry no reason; and nothing enforces that a composition holding `componentAbi` pins has a plane gate at all.

## Scope

58 files, +2144/−165, 7 commits, 3 devlog entries.

`slotReason` is declared as prose plus a Python tuple, matching every sibling closed `Text` set in the schema (`Object.kind`, `Executable.role`, `State.policy`, `NotificationBinding.role`); it never reaches the v5 binary encoding, so no format bump.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `just contracts_check` | Passed (206s), including the new gate |
| `just system_spec_check` | Passed — 21 named mutations refused |
| `just io_network_check` | Passed — the plane whose pins were removed boots |
| `just io_driver_authority_check` | Passed clean; **fails** on an injected permutation |
| `just devlog_check` | Passed — 266 entries, 266 indexed |
| `just fmt_check_all`, `just lint_all`, `just ruff` | Passed |
| Resolved-slot table, all 43 manifests | 1084 slots identical before/after |
| `generation.bin`, both affected compositions | Byte-identical before/after |

No QEMU plane gate was needed to prove the manifest change safe: the generation bytes every plane boots are proven identical by SHA-256 rather than by re-observing a boot. `io_network_check` and `io_driver_authority_check` were run anyway, because a pin was deleted from one plane and a permutation injected into the other.

## Roadmap side effects

`roadmap/README.md`'s index had drifted from its own track files, and the corrections are in this branch:

- It claimed **IO0–IO7 complete**, while `11-io-substrate.md` states IO4 is complete *only* for its exact-destination authority boundary and its network data plane is unfinished. That is the difference between a closed track and the one open gate on the demo critical path.
- It listed CP7's hosted-publication clause as the component platform's next open gate; `10-component-platform.md` closed it on 2026-08-26.

title: Native I/O substrate: IO0-IO7
body:
Adds the native I/O substrate track, IO0 through IO7: the architecture-neutral mechanisms that let supervised userspace drivers consume explicit hardware authority and expose typed semantic services, plus the three host verification layers that quantify over what a single QEMU boot cannot.

The load-bearing rule is **share I/O mechanisms, not device semantics**. `slime-root` constructs, grants, accounts, revokes, and reclaims hardware resources; it parses no virtio opcode, descriptor, packet, or TCP state.

> **Review history.** Round 2 found that in two slices the evidence layer *printed its conclusions instead of reaching them*, and that nine load-bearing defects sat in the trusted root and the drivers underneath. Round 3 closed B90, the last authority vestige the track left behind — and found that the fix's own first draft had reintroduced the same vacuity class it was deleting. Both rounds are detailed below: [round 2](#round-2-what-the-review-found), [round 3](#round-3-the-last-vestige-and-a-lesson-repeated).

## Slices

| Slice | What it adds | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| IO0 | Queue, request identity, epoch, and buffer-lease contract over C7/C9.2 | `just io_queue_check` |
| IO1 | Device/MMIO/IRQ/DMA authority with bounded accounting and reclamation on death | `just io_driver_authority_check` |
| IO2 | Userspace virtio-blk; the root's own block implementation deleted | `just io_block_check` |
| IO3 | Userspace virtio-net and a bounded `LinkDevice` under duplex readiness | `just io_link_check` |
| IO4 | Network service with exact destination authority | `just io_network_check` |
| IO5 | Two bounded Zutai models: all interleavings of IO0's lease/epoch rules and IO1's charge conservation | `just io_queue_model_check`, `just io_resource_model_check` |
| IO6 | Eighteen Kani harnesses over the shipped `slime-proto` wire arithmetic | `just kani_io_proofs` |
| IO7 | Thirteen Kani harnesses over the *device* trust boundary — the one input class no capability constrains | `just kani_virtio_proofs` |

Every QEMU gate is registered in `just sel4_gate_control_check`, which proves each fails on missing, reordered, or explicit failure evidence. Both model gates are in `contracts_check`.

The layers are complements, not substitutes: **one real schedule** (plane gates), **all interleavings of an abstraction** (models), **all values through the shipped Rust** (proofs — client side in IO6, device side in IO7). Each closes what the others structurally cannot: the models explicitly disclaim wire arithmetic, which is exactly what the Kani harnesses own; Kani drives one entry point, so liveness and two-party reachability stay the models'.

## Scope

284 files, +31906/−4721, 49 commits, 20 devlog entries.

New Zutai contracts: `io-queue`, `io-resource`, `block-authority`, `block` (v2), `link-device`, `network-destination`, `network-service`.

New components: `virtio-blk-driver`, `virtio-net-driver`, `network-service`, plus probe/intruder testkit pairs for each plane.

Net authority surface: **one capability kind and two rights bits removed** (round 3), against four kinds and four bits added by IO1 — the track ends with a smaller vocabulary than the sum of its additions.

## Round 2: what the review found

Two independent problem classes.

### The evidence class

A probe marker is a string, and nothing structurally required it to be *derived from an observation*. `sel4_gate_control_check` mutates declared markers to prove a gate fails on missing or reordered evidence — but a mutation test over literals only proves the checker reads strings. The gates and the probes agreed with each other while both disagreed with the machine.

`io-block-probe` printed seven fault-injection markers from a literal array, plus a restart and a stale-completion refusal. The driver has no fault, timeout, cancellation, or crash path, and the composition declares **zero supervision grants**, so nothing could restart it. It also claimed read/write/flush/geometry parity and durable readback while submitting only `OP_READ` — with the gate's own disk assertion checking the marker sector was byte-*unchanged*.

`io-network-probe` printed five reset/restart/reclamation markers against an **empty `sharedBufferBudget`**, no notifications, and no supervision: nothing to reclaim, no restart to observe. Its one real refusal was caused by a bug (below), which the gate read as "link reset" evidence.

Every literal is deleted. What replaced them is work actually performed: IO2 now writes a known 512-byte pattern, flushes, reads it back byte-for-byte, and the gate confirms it reached the backing image; five refusal arms are observed, including a write refused by a read-only ring. IO4 computes its authority figures from the decoded destination table and its refusal counts per arm. Marker pins moved with them — io-block 18→10, io-network 27→16, io-driver 15→16.

### The defect class

Nine, mostly guard/use splits in code whose own comments stated the invariant being broken.

| # | Defect |
|---|---|
| 1 | **IO0 ring lost update.** `put_header` rewrote all 128 bytes, so the client's `submit` wrote back a stale `submit_tail` and the driver's `complete` a stale `submit_head`. Both sides run concurrently against one mapping with no lock: a rolled-back `submit_tail` makes the driver **re-execute a request it already settled**. The module's own doc and the schema's two-cache-line split both declared single-writer ownership. |
| 2 | **First `OP_RECV` destroyed every live capability.** A service-wide epoch bumped on every receive, and every capability records the epoch at issue. One receive by any client invalidated that connection *and every other client's*. |
| 3 | **`authorizes_resolve` checked no rights bit and no budget** — holder and DNS name only. The intruder, granted `send` alone with `dnsRecordLimit = 0`, could resolve its own declared name. |
| 4 | **virtio-net indexed state by a client identity.** `request_id % IO_SLOTS`: the IO0 contract requires identities unique but *not dense*, so live ids 1 and 9 collided — an unreleasable DMA mapping, a request that never completes, and the first used entry settling the second request. B86's bug class one layer up, where B86's fix does not reach. |
| 5 | **`OP_RESET` dispatched before validation.** Reset exits the driver, so a payload with wrong magic, wrong version, or nonzero reserved bytes could kill it. |
| 6 | **Reclamation could lose the MMIO region permanently.** `map_child` unmaps before mapping, and the error path dropped the region after its frame was already unmapped. Since the base is driver-controlled, a driver could **permanently destroy its own device**. |
| 7 | **`begin_request` committed charges and then failed.** A queue mapping carries no lease, yet its identifier is handed to the driver as the `QUEUE_MAP` result — so the row was installed, the caller told to abandon it, and `destroy_dma_mapping` refused forever. |
| 8 | **`io_mmio_map` never transmitted the epoch it accepted.** The wrapper checked it *after* the root had mapped; the root substituted the table's own. Both sides theatre: a stale nonzero epoch created live MMIO authority. |
| 9 | **Device-refused used entries never settled.** Each refusal arm counted and continued, leaving a client lease and an IO1 charge live forever while an index overshoot repeated the refusal every pass. |

Plus fifteen smaller items: virtio-blk never adopted B87's used-ring helpers (that hardening covered net, not blk) and widened the device status byte verbatim, so `0xff` escaped as data; `block_io.rs` leaked its outstanding entry on four post-admission error paths; mediated MMIO was contained by QEMU's allocation order rather than by authority; `revoke_lease` had no production caller; `IRQ_WAIT_ACK` fabricated the arrival it acknowledged; two binding generators were registered in no gate; B88's remedy was left unapplied on its two sibling contracts; and `io-link-loopback` kept a dead function alive purely so `cargo-machete` would not flag a dependency — defeating the gate B85 exists for.

### Two bugs the review did not find

Both surfaced only because making IO2's evidence real required a second block device.

- **Device ordinals were inverted.** The root sorts transports into *reverse* physical order (`platform.rs:121-123`), so ordinal 0 is the **first** QEMU device, not the second that declaration order suggests. Diagnosed from a serial transcript showing `OP_WRITE` returning device IO_ERR — the write had reached the read-only disk. Exactly the B84 trap `AGENTS.md` warns about.
- **Slot-namespace collision.** The second peer endpoint at slot 2 resolved to nothing (`class=absent`): endpoint resolution requires no logical capability at the same relative number, and the probe's shared buffers occupy the low slots. Moved to slot 8, matching the convention `sel4-transfer` already uses for two-peer probes.

## Round 3: the last vestige, and a lesson repeated

B83 deleted `BLOCK TRANSACT`, the only operation that ever resolved a `Block` capability. The kind survived anyway — and it was not inert. Admission still derived `SERVICE_BLOCK` from a `Block` grant, so a holder that did not declare service `8` failed decode; two launch paths still assigned per-device ordinals to `Block` grants; the typed entry was still materialized, narrowable, and transferable. Nothing could resolve it: `resolve_block` had no caller outside its own module's tests, and no root label mapped to service 8. That is the exact shape `docs/capability-matrix.md` Grammar rule 2 forbids — enforcement machinery naming no operation.

B90 is now closed by deleting it: the kind, both rights bits, `SERVICE_BLOCK`, `BlockRights`, `resolve_block`, and both duplicated ordinal counters. `RIGHT_ALL` falls by exactly 3072. Wire discriminant 4, service id 8, and bits 10/11 are **reserved, never reassigned** — each is an ABI a component may still name.

**Two premises in the original backlog entry were wrong**, and correcting them is what made deletion the cheap option:

- B90 called full deletion "blocked on roadmap invariant 7: the bounded rollback window must still *decode* the `x86_64-qemu-virtio` generation." Invariant 7 says the opposite — a superseded format "counts as failed: the root refuses it (`UnsupportedVersion`...) rather than migrating it." `Generation::decode` implements that at the header, before any capability table is read, so an old generation never reaches the kind. The misreading came from a genuine terminology collision: P0's "bounded decoding of existing x86 artifacts" refers to legacy *component and kernel images*, which really do retain their meaning.
- B90 claimed `capability_rights_valid` *requires* both block rights, making the vestige able to refuse a generation. The predicate is `rights & required != 0` — either bit alone passes, and always did.

The real coupling was never rollback: it was the frozen CP1 baseline chain, which B83's own deferred follow-ups had already assigned to "the CP1 fixture's own migration." That migration is done here. The baseline is **not re-blessed** — it is evidence precisely because it is never regenerated — so its three grants are excused by a named `RETIRED_CAPABILITY_KINDS` exemption beside the existing `KNOWN_DEAD_BINDINGS` precedent, with guards that refuse an entry covering nothing and a kind that has become spellable again.

The partition test `declared_rights_partition_into_manifest_declarable_and_root_only` also now enumerates **all twelve** declared kinds. It previously named nine, omitting IO1's four — so `NOT_MANIFEST_DECLARABLE` meant "rejected for those nine" while bits 4–7 sat in it and real IO grants declared them anyway. Those four bits are now in `MANIFEST_DECLARABLE`, where the grants that spell them always implied they belonged.

### The lesson: a retirement silently defangs the mutations that named it

A five-lens read-only reviewer panel (canonical, correctness, security, convention, gate-integrity) reviewed the cutover. Verdicts: three *correct*, two *incorrect*; **no P0, no P1, no security defect**. Eleven findings applied, every one verified by mutation or probe before being acted on. The two that matter:

**Four negative controls had gone vacuous** — the same class the cutover had already fixed once, for the corpus-coverage arm, and then failed to look for elsewhere. Each mutated a spec using the now-unspellable `block`/`blockWrite`, so each was refused by a *membership* check before reaching the rule it named. All four gates still passed, reporting their usual refusal counts. Fixed by naming live vocabulary, each confirmed by instrumenting the gate to print its actual refusal reason:

| Arm | Was refused as | Now refused as |
|---|---|---|
| `unsorted_capability_kinds` | unknown kind `block` | `provides: must be sorted` |
| `undeclared_device` | unknown device kind `block` | `'input' appears in neither provides nor requires` |
| `rights_outside_kind` | unknown right `blockWrite` | `rights do not match capability kind endpoint` |
| corpus coverage arm | *spec required nothing at all* | a required kind nothing in the corpus provides |

**And the fix's own exemption shipped two defects of the same family.** Its non-vacuity guard was per-*set*, so a second bogus entry rode along on `block`'s coverage unnoticed — `{"block","neverExisted"}` exited 0. Worse, `check_retired_kinds`'s second assertion was a tautology: it re-tested the predicate the filter had already applied, so its `fail` branch was unreachable while its docstring advertised it as load-bearing. The first repair — reading the untouched fixture instead — was **also** unreachable, as round 2 of the panel caught: `declared` is built from the same grant list the stripped entries came out of, so it fires only on a duplicate grant name, which `system_spec.py` refuses independently. Exhaustive enumeration confirmed zero firings with unique names. It is now deleted rather than rewritten a third time, and the docstring cites the two checks that *can* fail.

Nine fault injections, each reverted, confirm every surviving guard fails closed with its intended message — including that mistyping the exemption set now reports the exemption error rather than a baseline divergence that would tempt someone to re-bless the frozen fixture.

## IO2's cutover is complete

All eight block-holding compositions — `sel4-storage`, `sel4-store`, `sel4-rollback`, `sel4-replay`, `sel4-generation`, `sel4-filesystem`, `sel4-recovery`, `sel4-transfer` — reach their devices through the userspace driver over IO0 rings, each gated on generation-declared per-ring rights (`contracts/block-authority/v1`). B83 then deleted `slime-root`'s virtio-blk command/descriptor implementation, `console.rs::serve_block_transact`, the `ConsoleKind::BlockTransact` label, and the `block_transact*` runtime wrappers. B90 finished the job by deleting the authority vocabulary they had left behind. The parser survives only as `boot_selector_block.rs` under `#[cfg(slime_boot_selector)]`, serving the immutable selector's pre-admission bootstrap read.

`contracts/block-authority/v1` is a genuinely independent contract, not a rename: its `rightRead`/`rightWrite` are a `u16` vocabulary (values 1 and 2) that never shared the retired generation bits' positions. Only the human-readable manifest spellings are reused, which the builder maps explicitly. Deleting the generation bits therefore could not, and did not, weaken per-ring storage authority.

The two-disk planes were the last mechanism gap: IO1 bound one driver instance to one device by literals. B84 declared a per-instance device ordinal in the IO1 budget and threaded it through every per-device identity.

## IO7: the device is untrusted input

IO0–IO6 all quantify over inputs arriving from a **client** — across a capability, through a generated codec, validated before use. None of it constrains the bytes a **device** writes into shared memory, under no capability at all. That input class was checked by nothing, and two real defects were sitting in it (B86, B87). Neither was reachable under any plane gate, and that is structural: **a plane observes only the schedule its own device produces**, and QEMU's virtio device is well behaved. No client-side gate reaches this code either — `io-link-intruder` is a *client*, and no client can forge a used-ring entry.

Three pure helpers now own the rules, with seven host tests and thirteen Kani harnesses over symbolic slot depth. Eight source mutations each produce a counterexample.

Round 2 strengthened this: the runt lower bound was first written by importing `slime_proto::link_device::MIN_FRAME_BYTES` into `virtio_mmio.rs`, which **broke the Kani gate** — `verification/virtio-proofs` points `[lib] path` at that file so verified and shipped source cannot drift, and that only holds while it imports nothing but `core`. It was also backwards as layering: this module is the virtio-mmio transport, and a minimum frame size is a link-protocol fact. The minimum is now a parameter, so the three affected harnesses quantify over it symbolically — they hold for **every** minimum a link protocol could declare, not just 60.

## Three Zutai-rule repairs

- **B88.** `contracts/network-destination/v1/schema.zt` always declared complete layouts and the Python renderer always emitted their offsets — but the Rust renderer emitted only scalars, so the decoder reached all twenty-two fields through hard-coded byte literals, and its own test encoder restated them. Two copies agreeing with each other, checked against the contract by nothing. Offsets are now generated. Round 2 applied the same remedy to `block-authority` and `io-resource`, which the original pass had left with the identical defect.
- **B89.** The same shape one level up: **fourteen** renderers each carried a byte-identical 82-line copy of the codec block, which had already drifted (`fabric-qos` and `fabric-time` emitted `expect("generated fabric-stream layout")`, naming the contract they were copied *from*). `wire.codec` now owns the emitters — **1382 lines deleted, 189 added** — with every generated artifact verified byte-identical across the migration.
- **B90's generated half.** Retiring the kind meant editing `contracts/generation/v5/{vocab/rights.zt,gen_rust.zt}` and regenerating, never touching the outputs. Both emitters had to lose `block` together, or the Python and Rust bindings would disagree about the vocabulary; `generate-boot-bindings.py --check` and a constant-for-constant comparison confirm they did.

## What this does **not** claim

Round 2 rewrote this section against the artifacts; several prior entries here were themselves overstatements.

- **IO4 implements no packet framing.** Ethernet, ARP, IPv4, ICMP, UDP, TCP, and DNS transport are on the explicit not-implemented list. The prior claim of "bounded IPv4/ARP/ICMP/UDP and a bounded TCP state machine" described code that does not exist; IO4 terminates at a structured capability service enforcing exact destination authority. The DHCP/SLAAC/NDP "declared and refused" claim is **withdrawn** — no contract declares them, so the stated "implementation change rather than contract change" benefit did not exist.
- **IO4 enforces three of eight per-destination bounds.** Socket, listener, and DNS-record ceilings are charged per holder from the generation. `queue_depth`, `byte_budget`, `timer_budget`, `retry_limit`, and `reconnect_limit` are decoded and unenforced.
- **IO4 demonstrates no backend independence.** `io-link-loopback` performs zero protocol operations, so the service is attached to no backend; the property was vacuous rather than demonstrated.
- **IO2 proves no fault injection, restart, or durability.** The driver has no cancellation or crash path and the plane has no supervision grant. Readback is same-boot, confirmed against the backing image; fresh-boot durability is not claimed.
- **IO3's link intruder proves binding refusal only.** The grant vocabulary expresses endpoint send/recv rights but no per-operation LinkDevice rights, so a rights-caused *operation* denial cannot be spelled there today.
- **B90 booted no seL4 plane.** Every deleted symbol was unreachable from all 40 compositions — no composition declares a `Block` grant, and the builder refuses every target profile whose fixtures do — so the host, contract, and spec gates cover the surfaces that changed. But "no plane regressed" is inferred from that reachability argument, not observed.
- **Reserved positions are pinned positively, not negatively.** Tests assert bits 10/11/17 are outside `RIGHT_ALL` and rejected by every kind; no test feeds a generation carrying discriminant 4 and asserts the exact refusal. A gap in evidence, not in behavior.
- **No physical containment.** Every slice is trusted-DMA on QEMU. No IOMMU exists here; H4 owns AMD-IOMMU proof and a future Arm milestone owns any SMMU proof.
- **No physical qualification.** Framework and Raspberry Pi 5 link/storage evidence remains H6/H12/RP work.
- **IO7 proves three functions, not the driver.** That `drain_used` *calls* them is argued by construction and pinned by `io_link_check`. No adversarial device exists in-tree, so the refusal arms are proved over all values but **never observed on a booted plane**.
- **IO5/IO6 boundaries** are stated in the roadmap: the models are not refinement proofs, and no `slime-root` code is Kani-covered.

## Verification

Every gate below was run locally at `HEAD` and passed:

```
just io_queue_check                 round trip, backpressure, late completion, reset epoch, slice refusal
just io_driver_authority_check      exact mediated MMIO, bounded IRQ authority, ungranted denial
just io_block_check                 computed operations, byte readback, async identity, refusal arms
just io_link_check                  duplex readiness, replenishment, reset, restart, authority
just io_network_check               exact authority, per-destination budgets, structured denials
just sel4_gate_control_check        45 gates reject 1748 mutated transcripts and layouts
just sel4_boot_layout_check         31 plane layouts match their fixtures
just generation_check               two isolated builds produce byte-identical generation and boot store
just system_spec_check              2 systems derived from their frozen baselines, 20 mutations refused
just component_spec_check           57 records, 43 mutations refused
just architecture_contract_check    target and executable-artifact contracts
just test_sel4_root                 211/211 across 19 modules
just test_host                      all suites, including 7 virtio_mmio device-boundary tests
just contracts_check                every generator's own --check agrees, both new ones registered
just kani_io_proofs                 18 harnesses verified
just kani_virtio_proofs             13 harnesses verified
just fmt_check_all / lint_all / machete / ruff / typos / devlog_check
```

`just machete` is green *honestly* now — the dead function propping up `io-link-loopback`'s `slime-proto` dependency is gone, which is the property B85 was filed to keep.

`just test_sel4_root` stays at 211 because round 3 **rewrote** the six affected tests around surviving kinds rather than deleting them; the test-name set is unchanged in both directions.

## Follow-ups recorded, not silently dropped

- Five of eight IO4 per-destination bounds remain decoded and unenforced.
- IO4 implements no packet framing, and `io-link-loopback` opens no queue.
- IO2 has no supervision grant, so restart and stale-completion behaviour are unproved there, as is fresh-boot durability.
- No adversarial device exists in-tree, so IO7's refusal arms are never observed on a booted plane. A fake virtio backend publishing odd ids and overstated lengths would close that gap.
- `io-link-intruder` remains capability-less pending per-operation link rights in the grant vocabulary.
- Bits 12–15 (`storeRead`, `storeWrite`, `healthConfirm`, `bootUpdate`) are now the *only* named-but-ungated rights left — residue of the retired custom kernel, a different retirement with different fixtures. B90 deliberately did not touch them.
- `scripts/check/check-generation.py` holds a third hand-written copy of the capability-kind and service vocabulary and still knows nothing of IO1's four kinds or `SERVICE_CLOCK`/`SERVICE_IO_RESOURCE` — B59-class follow-on, now with a named wider gap.
- The three frozen storage component records and their four `.layout` fixtures remain; B83's deferred item for them is narrower (grants gone, identities not) but not closed.
- `docs/capability-matrix.md` and `contracts/store/v1/README.md` are prose checked only by review. B90 falsified an authority claim in the latter and a reviewer caught it, not a gate — a second instance strengthening the case for a check that compares documented gate status against the rights some operation actually checks.
- `wire.rust`'s `WireField` still lacks `byteArray`, and `r.WireField` is now referenced by nothing. `fabric-operation` and `fabric-call` keep local emitters because their `constName` hard-codes a prefix.
- `serve_instance_graph` remains untestable pending a seL4 object-invocation seam (B61); marker expectations are Python literals rather than blessable fixtures (B63).
- Both Kani gates stay outside `contracts_check` and every aggregate gate: those must keep passing on a machine with no Kani closure.

With B90 closed, `roadmap/00-backlog.md`'s **Open section is empty**.

title: refactor(slime/sha256): back digests with RustCrypto sha2
body:
Replaces two independent hand-written FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 implementations with a single facade over RustCrypto's `sha2`.

`boot_contracts::sha256` is now a newtype over `sha2::Sha256` and is the workspace's only hasher. `components/runtime/src/sha256.rs` is deleted; `slime_rt::sha256` re-exports `boot_contracts::sha256::digest`. The public surface — `Sha256::{new, update, finalize}`, `Sha256::default()`, free `digest(&[u8]) -> [u8; 32]` — is unchanged, so none of the ~25 call sites across `boot-contracts`, `slime-root/src/boot_selector.rs`, and the four probes moved. Net −216/+107 lines, ~230 of unaudited crypto removed.

`sha2 0.10.9` was already resolved transitively via `ed25519-dalek` and already covered by `deny.toml`'s trust-chain policy, so `Cargo.lock` gains only a direct `boot-contracts -> sha2` edge at the same version. The dependency is non-optional (`sha256` is used unconditionally by every contract module, unlike `ed25519-dalek` behind `release-crypto`) and `default-features = false` keeps `std` off for the `no_std`, allocator-free component link.

## Digests are byte-identical

The eight-test module in `boot-contracts/src/sha256.rs` is untouched and now serves as the equivalence proof: NIST vectors, the one-million-`a` vector fed in unaligned 7-byte chunks, every split point, three-way splits, and every length adjacent to the padding boundary.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo check -p boot-contracts --all-features` | pass; lock edge confirmed at `0.10.9` |
| `just test_host` | pass; 8/8 `sha256::tests` among them |
| `just miri` | pass (400 s); `cpufeatures` reports the aarch64 SHA-2 extension absent under `cfg(miri)`, so the portable path is interpreted, never an `asm!` block |
| `just test_sel4_root` | 184/184 across 19 modules, covering `verify_directory_checksum` / `directory_root` |
| `just sel4_storage_check` | 9 markers; frozen `EXPECTED_DIGEST` matched on real aarch64 seL4 |
| `just sel4_store_check` | 14 markers + 4 refusal arms; content-hash lookup and append identity |
| `just sel4_transfer_check` | 11 markers; manifest digest, object closure, tamper refusal |
| `just generation_check` | byte-identical `generation.bin` across two isolated builds — the SHA-256-derived generation identity stays deterministic |
| `just fmt_check_all`, `just lint_all`, `just deny`, `just devlog_check` | pass |

## Notes

- `Sha256::new` is no longer `const` (`sha2::Sha256::new` is not a `const fn`). No caller used a const context; every one binds `let mut hasher = Sha256::new();` in a function body.
- `sha2`'s `force-soft` feature was deliberately **not** enabled — the default configuration passed Miri, so removing the hardware-accelerated backend on every real target would cost performance for no benefit.
- Devlog entry: `devlog/2026-08-27-sha256-rustcrypto-facade/index.md`.
